# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask commands` from the command registry. Don't edit it by hand: `cargo xtask check` fails if it differs from what the registry generates. -->

Every action a person or an agent can take in Beatlayer is a command in the registry (`crates/commands`). Menus, shortcuts, key and MIDI mapping, the agent API, and tests all run commands by the IDs below, so an action has one implementation however it's reached (decisions D16 and D17 in [the architecture](../02-architecture.md#decisions-log)).

Each command has:

- an **ID** that never changes, which key maps, MIDI maps, agents, and logs use;
- a **label**: what a person sees in menus and key-mapping lists;
- a **description** written for a model: what it does, when to use it, and what it changes;
- a **permission class**, which decides whether an agent asks first;
- **contexts**: the parts of the interface where a person reaches it, as [the UI parity reference](../ui-parity/README.md) names them;
- **default keys**: shortcuts from [the UI parity reference](../ui-parity/shortcuts.md), by ID, with any arguments they fix. The UI supplies the other arguments from the selection in the shortcut's context, a text field, or a gesture. A command Live has no shortcut for has no default keys;
- **arguments** and a **result** as JSON Schemas generated from the Rust types. An agent sends the arguments as a JSON object. The types they use are under [Types](#types);
- a **readback** for every command that isn't `read`: the read command or query that shows its effect, so an agent can check what it did ([Readback](#readback)).

## Permission classes

| Class | What a command in it may do | An agent |
|---|---|---|
| `read` | Changes nothing in the project or on disk: queries, and moving the keyboard focus or the view. | Runs it |
| `edit` | An undoable change to the project, or a preference that's trivially changed back. | Runs it |
| `destructive` | Removes project content (deleting tracks, clips, or devices), or loses work that undo can't restore: discards unsaved changes, overwrites a file, or quits. An agent asks first even when undo could restore the content. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |
| `external` | Reaches outside the project: files outside the project folder, the network, audio and MIDI devices, or other applications. | Asks the user first, unless the user has turned on autonomous mode for it |

## Readback

Anything an agent can set, it can read back. Each command that isn't `read` names where its effect shows: a read command and the field in its result, or the query tool's path for an object and the field in its full result. A query field is one the set saves for the object, or one of the song's overview. `cargo xtask commands` fails when a command that changes something names none, or names a field that isn't there. Each namespace's page has the rows for its commands.

## Types

The types the arguments and results use, with their JSON Schemas. A `$ref` such as `#/$defs/Ticks` names a type in this list.

### `AdaptiveGrid`

A zoom-adaptive grid setting: how far apart its lines stay on screen, from `widest` to `narrowest`. Each step is twice as dense as the one before. A new set uses `narrow`.

One of:

- `"widest"`: The fewest lines.
- `"wide"`: Fewer lines.
- `"medium"`: Between.
- `"narrow"`: More lines; a new set's setting.
- `"narrowest"`: The most lines.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A zoom-adaptive grid setting: how far apart its lines stay on screen, from `widest` to `narrowest`. Each step is twice as dense as the one before. A new set uses `narrow`.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "widest",
      "description": "The fewest lines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "wide",
      "description": "Fewer lines.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "medium",
      "description": "Between.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "narrow",
      "description": "More lines; a new set's setting.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "narrowest",
      "description": "The most lines.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `AddResult`

What `browser.add_to_arrangement` and `browser.load_selected` return.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | Audio tracks made for the files, top to bottom. |
| `clips` | array of [`PlacedClip`](#placedclip) | yes | The clips placed, in the order of the files. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What `browser.add_to_arrangement` and `browser.load_selected` return.",
  "properties": {
    "clips": {
      "description": "The clips placed, in the order of the files.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/PlacedClip"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "created_tracks": {
      "description": "Audio tracks made for the files, top to bottom.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/TrackId"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "created_tracks",
    "clips"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `AgentServerState`

What the agent server's commands return: its settings afterwards, without the token, which shows only in the Settings window.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | boolean | yes | Whether the server is switched on. |
| `url` | string | yes | The address agents connect to. |
| `clients` | array of [`AllowedAgent`](#allowedagent) | yes | The agents allowed to connect. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What the agent server's commands return: its settings afterwards, without the token, which shows only in the Settings window.",
  "properties": {
    "clients": {
      "description": "The agents allowed to connect.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/AllowedAgent"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "server": {
      "description": "Whether the server is switched on.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "url": {
      "description": "The address agents connect to.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "server",
    "url",
    "clients"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `AgentsPageSettings`

The Agents page's settings. The server's token and each allowed agent's are never reported, only whether the server has one.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | boolean | yes | Whether the agent server runs, as `agent.set_server` sets it. |
| `port` | integer from 0 to 65535 | yes | The port it listens on. |
| `url` | string | yes | The address agents connect to. |
| `token_stored` | boolean | yes | Whether the server has a token stored. |
| `clients` | array of [`AllowedAgent`](#allowedagent) | yes | The agents allowed to connect, with their autonomous mode. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The Agents page's settings. The server's token and each allowed agent's are never reported, only whether the server has one.",
  "properties": {
    "clients": {
      "description": "The agents allowed to connect, with their autonomous mode.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/AllowedAgent"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "port": {
      "description": "The port it listens on.",
      "format": "uint16",
      "maximum": 65535,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "server": {
      "description": "Whether the agent server runs, as `agent.set_server` sets it.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "token_stored": {
      "description": "Whether the server has a token stored.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "url": {
      "description": "The address agents connect to.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "server",
    "port",
    "url",
    "token_stored",
    "clients"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `AnalyzeResult`

What `perception.analyze` returns. A measure not asked for is null.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preview` | integer or null | yes | The preview analysed, or null for a range rendered for it. |
| `rendered` | [`Rendered`](#rendered) | yes | What was analysed. |
| `summary` | string | yes | The measurements in a few lines of text. |
| `loudness` | [`LoudnessResult`](#loudnessresult) or null | yes | Loudness and true peak. |
| `levels` | [`LevelsResult`](#levelsresult) or null | yes | Sample peak and RMS. |
| `spectrum` | [`SpectrumResult`](#spectrumresult) or null | yes | The octave-band spectrum. |
| `tempo` | [`TempoResult`](#temporesult) or null | yes | The tempo. |
| `key` | [`KeyResult`](#keyresult) or null | yes | The key. |
| `transients` | [`TransientsResult`](#transientsresult) or null | yes | The transients. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What `perception.analyze` returns. A measure not asked for is null.",
  "properties": {
    "key": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/KeyResult"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The key."
    },
    "levels": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LevelsResult"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Sample peak and RMS."
    },
    "loudness": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/LoudnessResult"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Loudness and true peak."
    },
    "preview": {
      "description": "The preview analysed, or null for a range rendered for it.",
      "format": "uint64",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "rendered": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Rendered",
      "description": "What was analysed."
    },
    "spectrum": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/SpectrumResult"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],

    },

      "description": "The measurements in a few lines of text.",
      "type": "string"

      "anyOf": [
        {
```

### `Appearance`

Which of a theme's two sets of colours is drawn (themes R3).

One of:

- `"light"`: Dark text on light panels.
- `"dark"`: Light text on dark panels, the default.
- `"follow-system"`: The operating system's mode, light or dark, as it changes.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Which of a theme's two sets of colours is drawn (themes R3).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "light",
      "description": "Dark text on light panels.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "dark",
      "description": "Light text on dark panels, the default.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "follow-system",
      "description": "The operating system's mode, light or dark, as it changes.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ApplicationState`

The open application, which is a chain of one or more tools.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tool` | string | yes | The chain's last tool. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip. |
| `input_notes` | integer, at least 0 | yes | How many input notes it keeps. |
| `range` | pair of [`Ticks`](#ticks) and [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The range it keeps. |
| `seed` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The seed of the chain's last tool. |
| `chain` | array of [`StepState`](#stepstate) | yes | The chain: each step's tool, settings and seed, in order. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The open application, which is a chain of one or more tools.",
  "properties": {
    "chain": {
      "default": [],
      "description": "The chain: each step's tool, settings and seed, in order.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/StepState"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "clip": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipId",
      "description": "The clip."
    },
    "input_notes": {
      "description": "How many input notes it keeps.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "range": {
      "description": "The range it keeps.",
      "maxItems": 2,
      "minItems": 2,
      "prefixItems": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        }
      ],
      "type": "array"
    },
    "seed": {
      "description": "The seed of the chain's last tool.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "tool": {
      "description": "The chain's last tool.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "tool",
    "clip",
    "input_notes",
    "range",
    "seed",
    "chain"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ArrangementState`

What the Arrangement View shows: every view command returns it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | [`TimeRange`](#timerange) | yes | The span of time across the track lanes, left edge to right edge. |
| `ticks_per_point` | number | yes | The zoom: ticks of song time per point of screen. |
| `scroll_y` | number | yes | How far the track lanes are scrolled down, in points. |
| `visible_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The tracks at least partly in view, top to bottom (the return tracks and Main, pinned at the bottom, are always in view and not listed). |
| `follow` | boolean | yes | Whether Follow is on. |
| `follow_paused` | boolean | yes | Whether Follow is on but paused, because the view was scrolled by hand while the song played; it resumes when playback starts or stops, or a click lands in the track lanes or the scrub area. |
| `overview` | boolean | yes | Whether the Overview shows above the rulers. |
| `optimize_height` | boolean | yes | Whether Optimize Height is on: every track fits in the lanes. |
| `optimize_width` | boolean | yes | Whether Optimize Width is on: the whole arrangement fits across. |
| `grid` | [`GridState`](#gridstate) | yes | The editing grid. |
| `insert_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the insert marker is. |
| `selected_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The selected tracks, top to bottom. |
| `selected_clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The selected clips (WP-1.8b), in the order they were selected. The editing commands act on these when there are any, and on the time selection otherwise. |
| `selected_locators` | array of [`LocatorId`](#locatorid) | yes | The selected locators (WP-6.24), in the order they were selected. The locator commands act on these. |
| `time_selection` | [`TimeRange`](#timerange) or null | yes | The selected span of time on the selected tracks, if any. |
| `folded_tracks` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | yes | The folded tracks. |
| `zoom_back_steps` | integer, at least 0 | yes | How many views `arrangement.zoom_back` can go back to. |
| `automation_mode` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Mode is on: each track shows its automation lane under its lane, with the device and parameter choosers. |
| `automation_arm` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Arm is on: while Arrangement Record runs, moving a control writes its values into the parameter's envelope. |
| `show_in_out` | boolean | yes | Whether the track headers show their In/Out column. |
| `show_volume` | boolean | yes | Whether the track headers show their volume, pan, and sends. |
| `show_return_tracks` | boolean | yes | Whether the return tracks' rows show in the lanes. |
| `automation_lanes` | array of [`AutomationLane`](#automationlane) | no | The parameter each track's automation lane shows, for the tracks whose lane isn't showing the default (their volume): the choosers' choice. `target` `null` means the lane draws no envelope. |
| `selected_breakpoint` | [`SelectedBreakpoint`](#selectedbreakpoint) or null | no | The breakpoint selected in that lane (WP-6.26), if any: `automation.select_breakpoint` sets it. |
| `selected_fade` | [`FadeHandleState`](#fadehandlestate) or null | no | The selected fade handle (WP-6.51), if any: Delete deletes its fade. |
| `selected_lane` | [`Lane`](#lane) or null | no | The automation lane that has the keyboard (WP-6.26): the one the last click, or Up and Down, selected, while Automation Mode is on. The keys of the automation editing spec's R20 to R26 act on its envelope. |
| `selected_take_lanes` | array of [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | no | The take lanes whose headers are selected (the comping spec, R26), in the order they were selected. Their tracks are selected tracks too. |
| `shown_take_lanes` | array of [`TrackId`](#trackid) | no | The tracks whose take lanes show (the comping spec, R24). |
| `time_selection_lanes` | array of [`Lane`](#lane) | no | The lanes the time selection covers: each a track's own lane, a take lane under it, or its automation lane (the automation editing spec, R1; the comping spec, R26). Empty when the selection names no lane. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What the Arrangement View shows: every view command returns it.",
  "properties": {
    "automation_arm": {
      "description": "Whether Automation Arm is on: while Arrangement Record runs, moving a control writes its values into the parameter's envelope.",
```

### `ArrowKey`

A direction a key points.

### `ArticulationOutput`

What an articulation sends when it becomes current.

One of:

- an object with `kind` = `"key"`, `key` (integer from 0 to 255), `velocity` (integer from 0 to 255): A key, 0 to 127, with a velocity, 1 to 127.
- an object with `kind` = `"controller"`, `controller` (integer from 0 to 255), `value` (integer from 0 to 255): A controller, 0 to 127, with a value, 0 to 127.

```json
          "description": "The key.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,

          "type": "integer"

        "key",
        "velocity"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "A controller, 0 to 127, with a value, 0 to 127.",

        "controller": {
          "description": "The controller.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "controller",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The value.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
```

### `ArticulationTrigger`

What makes an articulation current.

One of:

- an object with `kind` = `"none"`: None: only the Articulation control chooses it.
- an object with `kind` = `"key"`, `key` (integer from 0 to 255): A key, 0 to 127, matched on any channel at any velocity.
- an object with `kind` = `"controller"`, `controller` (integer from 0 to 255), `lowest` (integer from 0 to 255), `highest` (integer from 0 to 255): A controller, 0 to 127, with a range of values from a lowest to a highest.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
  "description": "What makes an articulation current.",
  "oneOf": [
    {

        "kind": {
          "const": "none",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "A key, 0 to 127, matched on any channel at any velocity.",
      "properties": {
        "key": {
          "description": "The key.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "key",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind",
        "key"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "A controller, 0 to 127, with a range of values from a lowest to a highest.",
      "properties": {
        "controller": {
          "description": "The controller.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "highest": {
          "description": "The highest value of the range.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "controller",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "lowest": {
          "description": "The lowest value of the range.",
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [

        "controller",
        "lowest",
        "highest"
      ],
      "type": "object"

  ]
}
```

### `AudioData`

An audio clip's data: the audio file it plays, named by content hash, and how it plays it. Times are seconds into the file. Every field but `media` is optional: a new clip plays the whole file once, at 0 dB, with no fades.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `media` | [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) | yes | The media file the clip plays, by content hash. |
| `detune` | number from -50 to 50 | no | The clip's Detune, in cents, from −50 to 50 (R2): 0 unless given. It shifts the clip's pitch in every mode but Re-Pitch (R10, R26). |
| `end` | number or null | no | The End marker: where in the file, in seconds, a clip whose loop is off stops playing, after the Start marker; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. |
| `fade_in` | number, at least 0 | no | The fade-in's length in seconds, from the clip's start in the Arrangement: 0 (no fade) unless given. |
| `fade_in_before` | number, at least 0 | no | How many seconds before the clip's start a crossfade (R24) begins its fade-in, over the clip that ends where this one starts: 0 unless this clip is the later of two crossfaded ones. The fade-in's length is then this much before the start and `fade_in` after it. |
| `fade_in_curve` | number from -1 to 1 | no | The fade-in's curve (the audio clips spec, R23), from −1 to 1: 0, the straight line, unless given. |
| `fade_out` | number, at least 0 | no | The fade-out's length in seconds, up to the clip's end in the Arrangement: 0 (no fade) unless given. |
| `fade_out_after` | number, at least 0 | no | How many seconds past the clip's end a crossfade (R24) ends its fade-out, under the clip that starts where this one ends: 0 unless this clip is the earlier of two crossfaded ones. The fade-out's length is then `fade_out` before the end and this much after it. |
| `fade_out_curve` | number from -1 to 1 | no | The fade-out's curve, from −1 to 1: 0 unless given. |
| `gain` | number, at least 0 | no | The clip's gain, as a linear gain: 1 (0 dB) unless given, 0.5 about −6 dB, and 0 silence (−∞ dB). Finite and 0 or more. |
| `high_quality` | boolean | no | The HiQ switch (R12): on unless given. On, the clip is resampled by a band-limited interpolator wherever it is read at another rate than 1. |
| `loop_end` | number or null | no | Where the loop brace ends in the file, in seconds, after its start; `null` (or nothing) for the end of the file. While the loop is on, the Start marker must be before it. |
| `loop_start` | number, at least 0 | no | Where the loop brace starts in the file, in seconds. 0 or more; 0 unless given. |
| `looping` | boolean | no | The Loop switch: whether the clip repeats its loop brace. Off unless given. |
| `ram` | boolean | no | The RAM switch (R11): off unless given. On, the clip's whole file is held in memory instead of streamed. |
| `signature` | [`TimeSignature`](#timesignature) or null | no | A warped clip's own time signature, the Clip View's Signature fields; `null` (or nothing) means the song's signature at the clip's start. |
| `start` | number, at least 0 | no | The Start marker: where in the file, in seconds, the clip starts playing. 0 or more; 0 unless given. |
| `tempo` | number or null | no | The clip's tempo in BPM, from 1 to 1,000: the speed of the file after the last warp marker (R2). Given whenever there are markers. |
| `tempo_leader` | boolean | no | The Lead/Follow switch (the warping spec, R43): whether this Arrangement clip leads the set's tempo instead of following it. Off unless given, a follower. Only a warped Arrangement clip can lead. |
| `transient_edits` | [`TransientEdits`](#transientedits) | no | The clip's edits to its file's detected transients (the warping spec, R23): none unless given. They belong to the file, so replacing the file drops them (R27). |
| `transpose` | integer from -48 to 48 | no | The clip's Transpose, in whole semitones, from −48 to 48 (R2): 0 unless given. It shifts the clip's pitch in every mode but Re-Pitch (R10, R26). |
| `warp` | boolean | no | The Warp switch (the warping spec, R1): off unless given. On, the clip follows the set's tempo through its warp map, and `start`, `end`, `loop_start` and `loop_end` are whole ticks of its contents, counted from the clip's 1.1.1, instead of seconds in the file. |
| `warp_markers` | array of [`WarpMarker`](#warpmarker) | no | The warp markers, in increasing order of both fields: a warped clip has at least one. Switching Warp off keeps them (R3). |
| `warp_mode` | [`WarpMode`](#warpmode) | no | The warp mode (the warp modes spec, R1): Beats unless given. An unwarped clip keeps it for when Warp goes back on. |
| `warp_settings` | [`WarpSettings`](#warpsettings) | no | Every mode's controls (R2): each at the table's default unless given. |

```json

  "description": "An audio clip's data: the audio file it plays, named by content hash, and how it plays it. Times are seconds into the file. Every field but `media` is optional: a new clip plays the whole file once, at 0 dB, with no fades.",

      "description": "The Warp switch (the warping spec, R1): off unless given. On, the clip follows the set's tempo through its warp map, and `start`, `end`, `loop_start` and `loop_end` are whole ticks of its contents, counted from the clip's 1.1.1, instead of seconds in the file.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "warp_markers": {
      "description": "The warp markers, in increasing order of both fields: a warped clip has at least one. Switching Warp off keeps them (R3).",

      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "warp_mode": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/WarpMode",
      "description": "The warp mode (the warp modes spec, R1): Beats unless given. An unwarped clip keeps it for when Warp goes back on."
    },
    "warp_settings": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/WarpSettings",
      "description": "Every mode's controls (R2): each at the table's default unless given."
    }
  },
  "required": [

  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `AudioSettings`

The audio device settings, as the Settings window's Audio page sets them and the preferences file keeps them. `None` means the platform's or the device's own choice.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `output_device` | string or null | yes | The output device's ID, or nothing for the system's default output device, which the stream then follows where the driver can. |
| `input_device` | string or null | yes | The input device's ID, or nothing for no input. |
| `sample_rate` | integer or null | yes | The sample rate in hertz, or nothing for the device's current rate, which leaves the device's own setting alone. |
| `buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size in frames, or nothing for the device's default. |
| `output_channels` | integer or null | yes | Output channels to open, or nothing for all the device has. |
| `driver_error_compensation_ms` | number | yes | Driver Error Compensation in milliseconds, two decimals, from -1000 to 1000: added to the device's reported latency when a recording is moved earlier to line up with what was played (WP-2.13). What `audio.status` returns.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `requested_buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size the settings asked for, in frames. |

### `AutomationRecordMode`

The mode an Arrangement recording writes its control moves in (the automation spec, R18): Touch, Live's; Latch; and Write (IMP-23). The names are Beatlayer's own.

One of:

- `"touch"`: Touch, Live's mode: a control writes its values while it is held.
- `"latch"`: Latch: the last value a control was moved to holds until the recording stops.
- `"write"`: Write: a control's envelope is written from where the recording started.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The mode an Arrangement recording writes its control moves in (the automation spec, R18): Touch, Live's; Latch; and Write (IMP-23). The names are Beatlayer's own.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "touch",
      "description": "Touch, Live's mode: a control writes its values while it is held.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "latch",
      "description": "Latch: the last value a control was moved to holds until the recording stops.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "write",
      "description": "Write: a control's envelope is written from where the recording started.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `AutomationTarget`

Which parameter of the track an envelope drives: `mixer` with a `param`, `send` with the return track it feeds (`to`), `device` with the device and its `param`, `chain` with a rack's chain and its mixer `param`, or `chain_send` with a drum rack's chain and the return chain it sends to (`to`), or `clip` with a sound setting (`param`) of the track's audio clips (Gain, Transpose, Detune, HiQ and the warp modes' controls). A MIDI clip's envelope can instead name a MIDI controller: `midi.cc` with its `number` (1 to 31 or 33 to 119), `midi.pitch_bend` or `midi.channel_pressure`.

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"mixer"`, `param` ([`MixerParam`](#mixerparam)): A control of the track's mixer.
- an object with `type` = `"send"`, `to` ([`TrackId`](#trackid)): The level of the track's send to a return track.
- an object with `type` = `"device"`, `device` ([`DeviceId`](#deviceid)), `param` ([`ParamId`](#paramid)): A parameter of a device in the track's chain.
- an object with `type` = `"chain"`, `chain` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)), `param` ([`MixerParam`](#mixerparam)): A control of a rack chain's mixer (WP-5.1, G2): the chain's Volume, Pan, or Chain Activator (`mute`: 1 muted, 0 not).
- an object with `type` = `"chain_send"`, `chain` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)), `to` ([`ChainId`](#chainid)): The level of a drum chain's send to a return chain of its rack (drum racks R6, G2).
- an object with `type` = `"clip"`, `param` ([`ClipParam`](#clipparam)): A sound setting of the track's audio clips (WP-4.8, the warp modes spec R28): a track's envelope for it drives the setting of every audio clip on the track as it plays, and a clip's envelope modulates it.
- an object with `type` = `"midi.cc"`, `number` (integer from 0 to 255): A continuous controller of a MIDI clip's MIDI Ctrl envelopes (WP-2.29), 1 to 31 or 33 to 119, from 0 to 127. Only a MIDI clip's envelope names it; a track has no automation for it.
- an object with `type` = `"midi.pitch_bend"`: A MIDI clip's pitch bend envelope, from −8192 to 8191, 0 at rest.
- an object with `type` = `"midi.channel_pressure"`: A MIDI clip's channel pressure envelope, from 0 to 127.

A MIDI clip's envelope can instead name a MIDI controller: `midi.cc` with its `number` (1 to 31 or 33 to 119), `midi.pitch_bend` or `midi.channel_pressure`.",

### `BouncedTrack`

The audio track a bounce made: its name, its mixer settings, its sends, its output routing, its mixer automation, and its clips.

| `name` | string | yes | The track's name: its source's name with " (Bounce)" after it. |

| `clips` | array of [`Clip`](#clip) | no | The clips on its Arrangement lane. |

| `output` | [`Output`](#output) | no | Where its audio goes. |
| `sends` | array of pair of [`TrackId`](#trackid) and number | no | Its sends, by return track: the level of each send that isn't at −∞ dB. |
| `slots` | array of pair of [`SceneId`](#sceneid) and [`Clip`](#clip) | no | The clips in its Session slots, by scene. |

```json
  "description": "The audio track a bounce made: its name, its mixer settings, its sends, its output routing, its mixer automation, and its clips.",
  "properties": {
    "automation": {
      "description": "Its mixer automation: one envelope per automated mixer control.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/BouncedAutomation"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "clips": {
      "description": "The clips on its Arrangement lane.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/Clip"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "mixer": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Mixer",
      "default": {
        "arm": false,
        "mute": false,
        "pan": 0.0,
        "solo": false,
        "volume": 1.0
      },
      "description": "Its mixer settings: its source's volume, pan, activator, and solo."
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The track's name: its source's name with \" (Bounce)\" after it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "output": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Output",
      "default": {
        "type": "default"
      },
      "description": "Where its audio goes."
    },
    "sends": {
      "description": "Its sends, by return track: the level of each send that isn't at −∞ dB.",
      "items": {
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "prefixItems": [
          {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/TrackId"
          },
          {
            "format": "double",
            "type": "number"
          }
        ],
        "type": "array"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "slots": {
      "description": "The clips in its Session slots, by scene.",
      "items": {
        "maxItems": 2,
        "minItems": 2,
        "prefixItems": [
          {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/SceneId"
          },
          {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/Clip"
          }
        ],
        "type": "array"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `Chain`

One chain of a rack: its own name, colour, info text and mixer, and its devices in signal order.

| `choke` | integer or null | no | The choke group a drum rack's chain is in, from 1 to 16, or none. |

### `ChainMixer`

A chain's mixer: `volume` (linear gain, 1 is 0 dB, 0 is -inf), `pan` (-1 left to 1 right), `enabled` (the Chain Activator) and `solo`. A MIDI effect rack's chains have no volume or pan.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | The Chain Activator: on in a new chain. A chain that's off adds nothing to its rack's output. |
| `pan` | number | no | From −1 (left) to 1 (right): centre in a new chain. |
| `solo` | boolean | no | Solo: while any chain of a rack is soloed, its unsoloed chains add nothing. |
| `volume` | number | no | Linear gain: 1 (0 dB) in a new chain. |

```json
}
```

### `ChainSelect`

How `chain.select` changes the selection.

One of:

- `"replace"`: Select only `chain`: a click.
- `"toggle"`: Add `chain` to the selection, or remove it: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click).
- `"range"`: Select every chain from the selected one to `chain`: Shift-click.
- `"previous"`: Select only the chain above the first selected one: Up.
- `"next"`: Select only the chain below the last selected one: Down.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How `chain.select` changes the selection.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "replace",
      "description": "Select only `chain`: a click.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "Add `chain` to the selection, or remove it: Cmd-click (Ctrl-click).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "range",
      "description": "Select every chain from the selected one to `chain`: Shift-click.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "previous",
      "description": "Select only the chain above the first selected one: Up.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "next",
      "description": "Select only the chain below the last selected one: Down.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ChangeSet`

What a command changed: whether the song settings (the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place) changed, whether the track list changed, and which tracks, scenes, clips, and devices were added, removed, or modified, keyed by ID. Every field is empty or false if nothing changed.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | boolean | yes | The song settings changed: the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place. |
| `layout` | boolean | yes | The track tree changed: a track was added, removed, or moved, so routing may have changed. |
| `tracks` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Tracks whose own settings changed: name, mixer, sends, the tracks inside a group, or the order of the device chain. Changes to a track's clips or to its devices' settings are listed under `clips` and `devices` instead. |
| `scenes` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Scenes that were added, removed, renamed, or moved. A scene whose clips changed only is listed under `clips`, not here. |
| `clips` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Clips that changed, including clips moved to another track or between the Arrangement and a Session slot. |
| `devices` | object of [`Change`](#change) by integer key | yes | Devices whose settings changed, including devices moved to another track. |

Every field is empty or false if nothing changed.",

```json
      "additionalProperties": false,

      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "layout": {
      "description": "The track tree changed: a track was added, removed, or moved, so routing may have changed.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "scenes": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Scenes that were added, removed, renamed, or moved. A scene whose clips changed only is listed under `clips`, not here.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    },
    "settings": {
      "description": "The song settings changed: the tempo map, the time-signature map, the crossfader, the Arrangement loop, or Solo in Place.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "tracks": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "Tracks whose own settings changed: name, mixer, sends, the tracks inside a group, or the order of the device chain. Changes to a track's clips or to its devices' settings are listed under `clips` and `devices` instead.",
      "patternProperties": {
        "^-?\\d+$": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Change"
        }
      },
      "type": "object"
    }

  "required": [
```

### `Channel`

One of the audio interface's channels: `mono` a single channel, or `pair` a stereo pair starting at it, counted from 1 (`{ "type": "pair", "channel": 3 }` is the pair 3/4).

One of:

- an object with `type` = `"mono"`, `channel` (integer from 0 to 65535): A single channel, counted from 1.
- an object with `type` = `"pair"`, `channel` (integer from 0 to 65535): A stereo pair: its first channel, counted from 1; the second is the next one.

```json
          "maximum": 65535,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"

        "type": {

          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "type",
        "channel"
      ],

    }

}
```

### `Clip`

A clip on a track's arrangement lane.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clip's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The clip's name, which may be empty. |
| `start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the clip starts in the arrangement. Never negative. |
| `length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the clip is. Always positive. |
| `mute` | boolean | yes | Whether the clip is switched off, so it stays in place but doesn't play. |
| `data` | [`ClipData`](#clipdata) | yes | What the clip plays. |
| `envelopes` | array of [`ClipEnvelope`](#clipenvelope) | no | The clip's envelopes (WP-3.15): one per parameter of its track it modulates, in target order. Empty for a clip with none, which is what a set saved before this package holds. |
| `groove` | [`GrooveId`](#grooveid) or null | no | The clip's groove (WP-6.19): one of the set's Groove Pool, or none. It changes when the clip's notes play, or where its audio plays, and nothing in the clip itself until it is committed. |
| `launch` | [`ClipLaunch`](#cliplaunch) | no | The clip's launch settings (WP-3.4), which only a Session clip's launching reads. The defaults for a clip saved without them. |
| `offset` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | no | How far into its contents a MIDI clip starts: its notes are placed from `start - offset`, and the part before the clip's start doesn't play. 0 (or left out) plays the contents from their beginning. Never negative. Splitting a MIDI clip or trimming its left edge changes it, so each part plays what it played before. An audio clip's is always 0: its Start marker moves instead, as Live's does. |
| `scale` | [`Scale`](#scale) | no | The clip's scale (WP-6.7): its Scale Mode switch, its root and its scale name. It never changes what the clip plays; it tells the rest of the set which keys belong. A clip off at C, in Major, writes nothing, so a set saved before the scales loads unchanged. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A clip on a track's arrangement lane.",
  "properties": {
    "data": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipData",
      "description": "What the clip plays."
    },
    "envelopes": {
      "description": "The clip's envelopes (WP-3.15): one per parameter of its track it modulates, in target order. Empty for a clip with none, which is what a set saved before this package holds.",

        "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipEnvelope"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "groove": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/GrooveId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The clip's groove (WP-6.19): one of the set's Groove Pool, or none. It changes when the clip's notes play, or where its audio plays, and nothing in the clip itself until it is committed."
    },
    "id": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipId",
      "description": "The clip's ID."
    },
    "launch": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/ClipLaunch",
      "description": "The clip's launch settings (WP-3.4), which only a Session clip's launching reads. The defaults for a clip saved without them."
    },
    "length": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "How long the clip is. Always positive."
    },
    "mute": {
      "description": "Whether the clip is switched off, so it stays in place but doesn't play.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The clip's name, which may be empty.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "offset": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "How far into its contents a MIDI clip starts: its notes are placed from `start - offset`, and the part before the clip's start doesn't play. 0 (or left out) plays the contents from their beginning. Never negative. Splitting a MIDI clip or trimming its left edge changes it, so each part plays what it played before. An audio clip's is always 0: its Start marker moves instead, as Live's does."
    },
    "scale": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Scale",
      "description": "The clip's scale (WP-6.7): its Scale Mode switch, its root and its scale name. It never changes what the clip plays; it tells the rest of the set which keys belong. A clip off at C, in Major, writes nothing, so a set saved before the scales loads unchanged."
    },
    "start": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks",
      "description": "Where the clip starts in the arrangement. Never negative."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "id",
    "name",
    "start",
    "length",
    "mute",
    "data"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `ClipEnvelope`

An envelope a clip carries for a parameter of its track: the parameter it modulates, its breakpoints, and whether it follows the clip's timeline (`linked`, the default) or runs once from the clip's start (`false`).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) | yes | The parameter it modulates: a control of the clip's track's mixer, a send, or a parameter of a device in its chain. |
| `envelope` | [`Envelope`](#envelope) | yes | Its breakpoints, in position order: positions are ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents, like a note's start. |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Whether an automation envelope drives its parameter: a control moved by hand while the clip plays turns it off until the clip launches again or Re-Enable Automation. Always true for a modulation envelope. |
| `kind` | [`EnvelopeKind`](#envelopekind) | no | Whether it modulates the parameter or sets it (WP-3.12). A clip can hold one of each kind for a parameter. |
| `linked` | boolean | no | Whether it follows the clip's region and loop (`true`, the Linked switch's default) or plays once from the clip's start (`false`). |

```json
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "target": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/AutomationTarget",

    "envelope"
  ],

}
```

### `ClipLaunch`

A Session clip's own launch settings (the Clip View's Launch panel, WP-3.4). They are saved with the clip, so they're part of the set and each change is one undo step; a clip without them has the defaults.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `follow` | [`FollowActions`](#followactions) | no | What the clip does by itself after it has played for a while (WP-3.10). |
| `legato` | boolean | no | Legato: the clip takes over the play position of the clip playing on its track when it launches. |
| `mode` | [`LaunchMode`](#launchmode) | no | What a press and a release of the clip's launch button do (WP-3.3). |
| `quantization` | [`LaunchQuantization`](#launchquantization) or null | no | The clip's own launch quantisation; `null` (left out) follows the global one, which Live's chooser calls "Global". |
| `velocity_amount` | number | no | How much the velocity of a note that launches the clip changes its volume, from 0 (none, the default) to 1 (100 %). |

### `ClipParam`

A sound setting of an audio clip: `gain` (linear, 1 is 0 dB), `transpose` (semitones), `sample_offset` (Beats only, in sixteenth notes, an envelope only), `detune` (cents), `high_quality` (the HiQ switch), `preserve`, `transient_loop_mode` and `transient_envelope` (Beats), `tones_grain_size`, `texture_grain_size` and `texture_flux`, `formants` and `complex_pro_envelope` (Complex Pro).

One of:

- `"gain"`: The clip's gain: a linear gain from silence (−∞ dB) to +24 dB.
- `"transpose"`: Transpose, in semitones, −48 to 48.
- `"sample_offset"`: Beats' Sample Offset (R30), in sixteenth notes, −8 to 8. It has no setting of its own: only an envelope or automation moves it.
- `"detune"`: Detune, in cents, −50 to 50.
- `"high_quality"`: The HiQ switch.
- `"preserve"`: Beats' Preserve, by its place in the list.
- `"transient_loop_mode"`: Beats' Transient Loop Mode, by its place in the list.
- `"transient_envelope"`: Beats' Transient Envelope, 0 to 100.
- `"tones_grain_size"`: Tones' Grain Size, in milliseconds.
- `"texture_grain_size"`: Texture's Grain Size, in milliseconds.
- `"texture_flux"`: Texture's Flux, in per cent.
- `"formants"`: Complex Pro's Formants, in per cent.
- `"complex_pro_envelope"`: Complex Pro's Envelope, 8 to 512.

```json
      "description": "Detune, in cents, −50 to 50.",
```

### `ClipViewState`

What the Clip View shows: which clip it is editing, the notes selected in it, its insert marker and time selection, its expression lanes, and the tab with the envelope it shows.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `visible` | boolean | yes | Whether the Clip View shows in the detail area. |
| `draw_mode` | boolean | yes | Whether Draw Mode is on (B): clicking the note area adds a note, and clicking a note removes it. |
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) or null | yes | The clip the note editor shows; `null` when none does. With several clips shown, the foreground clip. |
| `clips` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The clips the note editor shows, in the loop bars' order (Spec: multi-clip-editing R1, R2): none, one, or up to eight. |
| `loop_bars` | array of [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The loop bars selected, in the order of `clips`. |
| `focus_mode` | boolean | yes | Whether Focus Mode is on (Spec: multi-clip-editing R13). |
| `selected` | array of integer, at least 0 | yes | The selected notes of the foreground clip, by their place in its notes in order (by start, then pitch). |
| `clip_selections` | array of [`ClipEdit`](#clipedit) | yes | The selected notes of every clip shown, by clip; the foreground clip's are `selected` too. |
| `insert_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | yes | The insert marker, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents; `null` when there is none. |
| `time_selection` | array or null | yes | The time selection's start and end, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents; `null` when there is none. |
| `lane` | [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | The active lane: `velocity`, `chance` or `release_velocity`, whose controls the footer shows. |
| `lanes` | array of [`NoteField`](#notefield) | yes | The lanes shown under the note editor now, from the top: none while they are all hidden. |
| `lanes_hidden` | boolean | yes | Whether the Show/Hide All Expression Editors switch has hidden every lane. |
| `randomize` | [`RandomizeAmounts`](#randomizeamounts) | yes | The Randomize amounts of the three lanes. |
| `folded` | boolean | yes | Whether the note editor shows only the rows that hold notes (Fold, F). |
| `tab` | [`ClipTab`](#cliptab) | yes | The tab the Clip View shows. |
| `preview` | boolean | yes | Whether the Preview switch is on (Spec: step-recording R1): one switch for every MIDI clip's editor, kept between launches. |
| `envelope` | [`AutomationTarget`](#automationtarget) or null | yes | The parameter whose envelope the Envelopes tab shows; `null` when it shows none. |
| `filters` | [`NoteFilters`](#notefilters) | yes | Find and Select Notes: whether the filter bar shows, and every filter's settings, with which are on. |
| `envelope_breakpoint` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The breakpoint selected in the Envelope Editor (WP-6.26), if any: `clip.select_envelope_breakpoint` sets it. |
| `envelope_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) or null | no | The Envelope Editor's insert marker, in ticks from the beginning of the clip's contents (WP-6.26), which Left and Right move along the envelope; `null` until it has been moved. |

### `CollectFiles`

What happens to the audio files a clip or a set uses when it is saved to the browser (file-management R7): Collect Files on Export.

One of:

- `"always"`: Copy the files into the saved file's project. A new install's choice.
- `"never"`: Copy nothing: the saved file names each file where it is.
- `"ask"`: Ask first, with Copy, Don't Copy and Cancel.

```json
}
```

### `DetailState`

What the detail area's commands return, and `view.state` reports under `detail` (detail-views R17): which views show, where the focus is and how tall the Clip View is.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip_view` | boolean | yes | Whether the Clip View shows. |
| `device_view` | boolean | yes | Whether the Device View shows. |
| `alone_last` | [`DetailView`](#detailview) | yes | The view that showed alone last, which `view.switch_detail_view` brings back when neither shows. |
| `hidden` | array of [`DetailView`](#detailview) | yes | The views `view.toggle_detail_area` hid, which it brings back; empty when it hid nothing. |
| `clip_height` | number | yes | The Clip View's height in points at 100%, as it was set; it is squeezed in a window too short for it. |
| `expanded` | boolean | yes | Whether the Clip View is expanded to its largest height. |
| `focus` | [`DetailView`](#detailview) | yes | The view the detail area's keys go to while both show. |

```json
      "$ref": "#/$defs/DetailView",

      "description": "The Clip View's height in points at 100%, as it was set; it is squeezed in a window too short for it.",

      "type": "boolean"
    },

      "description": "Whether the Device View shows.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "expanded": {
      "description": "Whether the Clip View is expanded to its largest height.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "focus": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/DetailView",
      "description": "The view the detail area's keys go to while both show."
    },
    "hidden": {
      "description": "The views `view.toggle_detail_area` hid, which it brings back; empty when it hid nothing.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/DetailView"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
```

### `DetailView`

One of the detail area's two views.

One of:

- `"clip"`: The Clip View, which edits the selected clip.
- `"device"`: The Device View, which shows the selected track's devices.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "One of the detail area's two views.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "clip",
      "description": "The Clip View, which edits the selected clip.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "device",
      "description": "The Device View, which shows the selected track's devices.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Device`

A device in a track's chain: a native instrument or effect, or a plug-in.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device's ID. |
| `name` | string | yes | The name the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is on: the device's own name until a preset or Rename gives it another. |
| `kind` | [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) | yes | What the device is. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether the device is switched on. A device that's off passes its input through unchanged. |
| `params` | array of pair of [`ParamId`](#paramid) and number | yes | Parameter values the user has set, in the parameter's own units. Every value is finite. Parameters not listed keep their defaults.  They serialise as a list of `[parameter, value]` pairs, since some formats can't key a map by number. |
| `articulations` | array of [`Articulation`](#articulation) | no | An Articulation Map's articulations, in order (WP-6.47; the articulation map spec, R2): each with a name, a trigger, up to four outputs and a channel. Empty for every device that isn't an articulation map, and left out of the saved set then. |
| `b_active` | boolean | no | Whether the device's B state is the active one, whose values [`params`](Self::params) holds (device compare R1). Left out of the saved set while A is active. |
| `chains` | array of [`Chain`](#chain) | no | A rack's chains, in order (WP-5.1). Empty for every device that isn't a rack, and left out of the saved set then, so sets saved before racks load unchanged. |
| `configured` | array or null | no | The plug-in parameters the device's panel holds, in order (clap-hosting R5, configure mode): the list Configure Mode edits, saved with the set. Left out until it's set: until then all of a plug-in's parameters are configured when it has no more than [`CONFIGURE_THRESHOLD`], and none when it has more (manual 24.1). Native devices never set it. |
| `external` | [`External`](#external) or null | no | The device's routing to external hardware, if its type declares one (WP-5.34): an external instrument's output port and channel, the interface inputs it comes back on, and its Hardware Latency. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |
| `floating` | boolean | no | Whether the device floats in a window of its own rather than showing in the Device View (IMP-14, WP-2.5b), where its place in the chain shows as a strip. Only native devices float. Left out of the saved set while docked. Where its window sits isn't part of the document: moving or resizing a window isn't an undo step ([`WindowFrame`]). |
| `layers` | [`Layers`](#layers) | no | A multisampler's layers and the options of its layer list (WP-5.13, the multisampler spec, R2). Left out of the saved set for a device that holds none. |
| `macros` | [`RackMacros`](#rackmacros) | no | A rack's macros' settings and mappings (WP-5.4; the macros spec, R17). Left out of the saved set while it has neither. |
| `mappings` | array of [`Mapping`](#mapping) | no | The parameters a modulator maps, one per slot (the modulation spec, R19). Left out of the saved set for a device that maps none. |
| `media` | array of [`ContentHash`](#contenthash) or null | no | The media the device plays, by content hash, one entry per sample slot (WP-2.16, WP-5.17): the sampler's sample is slot 0, the eight-slot drum sampler's slots are 0 to 7. The media store holds each like a clip's audio (the sampler spec, R11). A slot with no sample is `None`, and the list never ends in one. Left out of the saved set for a device that plays none; a set saved before slots existed holds one hash, which loads as slot 0. |
| `midi_sidechain` | [`MidiSidechain`](#midisidechain) or null | no | The device's MIDI sidechain input, if its type declares one (the routing spec, R32): a MIDI track whose notes and channel messages the device hears beside its audio. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |
| `other_params` | array or null | no | The values of the state that isn't active, in the same form as [`params`](Self::params) (device compare R1, R10). `None` while the two states are equal, as a new device's are, and left out of the saved set then. Use [`other_params`](Self::other_params) to read it. |
| `own_name` | string | no | The device's own name, such as `Auto Filter`, which the title bar shows while Show Preset Name is off. Empty while it's the same as [`name`](Self::name), and left out of the saved set then. |
| `plugin` | [`PluginState`](#pluginstate) or null | no | A plug-in's own state and where it was loaded from (WP-2.6), as last saved with the set. Left out of the saved set for a native device, and for a plug-in until the set is first saved with it. |
| `preset_name` | string or null | no | The name of the preset the device holds (the plug-in list spec, R5): the Beatlayer device preset last loaded into it or saved from it, or else the program name the plug-in's format reported. Left out of the saved set while there is none, so a device saved before this package loads with none. |
| `role` | [`DeviceRole`](#devicerole) | no | Where it goes in a chain: MIDI effects, then the instrument, then audio effects. Audio effects aren't marked in the saved set. |
| `sample_edits` | array of [`SampleEdit`](#sampleedit) | no | The edits made to the sample in slot 0 (WP-5.15, IMP-28; the multisampler spec, R55): applied in order to the media, which the file is never written for. A multisampler's layers hold their own. Loading another sample clears them. Left out of the saved set while there are none. |
| `shape` | array or null | no | The breakpoints of a Shaper's shape (R23); `None` plays the default shape. Left out of the saved set while it is the default. |
| `show_preset_name` | boolean | no | Whether the title bar shows the preset's or the given name (on, as a new device is) or the device's own name: the context menu's Show Preset Name. Left out of the saved set while on. |
| `sidechain` | [`Sidechain`](#sidechain) or null | no | The device's sidechain input, if its type declares one (WP-2.19b): where its detector can listen other than its own input. Left out of the saved set for a device without one. |
| `slices` | array of integer, at least 0 | no | Manual slice markers in frames into the sample, for devices that support manual slicing (WP-5.15b, Simpler). Kept in increasing order of frame. Left out of the saved set when empty. |
| `warp` | [`DeviceWarp`](#devicewarp) | no | Warp settings for devices that play warped media (WP-5.15b, Simpler). Left out of the saved set when default. |

### `DeviceDescription`

What a kind of device is to the framework: its parameters' descriptors, in the order its generic UI and agents list them, and its layout.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `params` | array of [`ParamDescriptor`](#paramdescriptor) | yes | Its parameters. |
| `layout` | [`DeviceLayout`](#devicelayout) | yes | Where its controls and display cells sit (IMP-14). |
| `menu_options` | array of [`ParamId`](#paramid) | no | The switches the device lists as its own items in its Show Options menu, after Save as Default Preset (C-DEVICE-015), in this order. They are parameters like any other, but the layout places no control for them. |
| `title_switch` | [`ParamId`](#paramid) or null | no | The switch the device draws in its title bar instead of its panel (L-DEV-004): Use Current Scale, on the five scale-aware devices. It is a parameter like any other, which the layout places no control for. |
| `views` | array of string | no | The views its display offers, such as `Transfer Curve`, the first being the one it starts in; empty for a display with one view. Which is shown is view state (`device.set_display_view`). |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "What a kind of device is to the framework: its parameters' descriptors, in the order its generic UI and agents list them, and its layout.",
  "properties": {
    "layout": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/DeviceLayout",

    },

      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Its parameters.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/ParamDescriptor"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "title_switch": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ParamId"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "The switch the device draws in its title bar instead of its panel (L-DEV-004): Use Current Scale, on the five scale-aware devices. It is a parameter like any other, which the layout places no control for."
    },
    "views": {
      "description": "The views its display offers, such as `Transfer Curve`, the first being the one it starts in; empty for a display with one view. Which is shown is view state (`device.set_display_view`).",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "params",
    "layout"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `DeviceDisplay`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `readings` | array of [`DisplayReading`](#displayreading) | yes | Its single readings. |
| `view` | string or null | no | The view the display is showing, for a device whose display has views. |

```json
    "readings"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `DeviceFrame`

One device as the Device View shows it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `title` | string | yes | What its title bar reads: its preset's or given name while Show Preset Name is on, otherwise its own name. |
| `name` | string | yes | Its own name, such as `Auto Filter`. |
| `kind` | [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) | yes | What it is. |
| `role` | [`DeviceRole`](#devicerole) | yes | Where it goes in a chain. |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether it's switched on. |
| `takes_sample` | boolean | yes | Whether its type plays one sample, so a sample dropped on it loads into it (`device.load_sample`, WP-2.16). |
| `swaps_to_snapshot` | boolean | yes | Whether its type is the drum sampler, whose context menu offers the swap to Simpler and Save as Default Pad (`device.swap_to_snapshot`, one-shot drum sampler R23). |
| `show_preset_name` | boolean | yes | Whether its title shows its preset's or given name. |
| `folded` | boolean | yes | Whether it's folded to its title bar. |
| `expandable` | boolean | yes | Whether it has an expanded part, which its title bar's expand toggle shows and hides (L-DEV-004; WP-5.42). |
| `expanded` | boolean | yes | Whether its expanded part is shown. Never while it has none. |
| `floating` | boolean | yes | Whether it floats in a window of its own, its place in the chain a strip (WP-2.5b). |
| `b_active` | boolean | yes | Whether its B state is the active one, which the title bar marks "(B)" (device compare R5). |
| `configure` | boolean | yes | Whether the device is in Plug-In Configure Mode (clap-hosting R5, WP-5.40): its title bar's Configure switch is lit. View state, never saved with the set. False for a device that isn't a plug-in. |
| `selected` | boolean | yes | Whether it's the selected device. |
| `hot_swap` | boolean | yes | Whether it's the device being hot-swapped. |
| `sidechain` | [`SidechainSection`](#sidechainsection) or null | yes | Its sidechain section, if it has a sidechain input (WP-2.19b). |
| `display_view` | string or null | no | The view its display shows, if its display has views (WP-5.43): one of its description's `views`. |
| `external` | [`ExternalSection`](#externalsection) or null | no | Its routing to hardware, if it is an external device (WP-5.34). |
| `midi_sidechain` | [`MidiSidechainSection`](#midisidechainsection) or null | no | Its MIDI sidechain section, if it has a MIDI sidechain input (WP-5.27). |
| `modulator` | [`ModulatorFrame`](#modulatorframe) or null | no | For a modulator, what it maps and which Map button is armed (WP-5.10). |
| `multisampler` | [`MultisamplerState`](#multisamplerstate) or null | no | A multisampler's views and selected layers (WP-5.13, R30); left out for any other device. |
| `panel` | [`DevicePanel`](#devicepanel) or null | no | Its parameters and layout, for the generic UI; left out for a device whose type doesn't describe them. |
| `rack` | [`RackFrame`](#rackframe) or null | no | A rack's frame: its views, its chain list and the selected chain's devices (WP-5.2). None for a device that isn't a rack. |

### `DeviceId`

The ID of a device: a positive integer, unique within the project and never reused.

Type: integer, at least 1.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The ID of a device: a positive integer, unique within the project and never reused.",
  "format": "uint64",
  "minimum": 1,
  "type": "integer"
}
```

</details>

### `DeviceKind`

What a device is.

One of:

- an object with `native` (object with `device_type` (string)): A device built into Beatlayer.
- an object with `plugin` (object with `format` ([`PluginFormat`](#pluginformat)), `plugin_id` (string)): A plug-in.
- an object with `rack` (object with `kind` ([`RackKind`](#rackkind))): A rack (WP-5.1): a device that holds [`Device::chains`].

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What a device is.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A device built into Beatlayer.",
      "properties": {
        "native": {
          "properties": {
            "device_type": {
              "description": "The device type's stable identifier, such as `beatlayer.utility`.",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "device_type"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "native"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A plug-in.",
      "properties": {
        "plugin": {
          "properties": {
            "format": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/PluginFormat",
              "description": "The plug-in's format."
            },
            "plugin_id": {
              "description": "The plug-in's identifier in its format: a CLAP ID, a VST3 class ID, an Audio Unit's type, subtype, and manufacturer, or an LV2 URI.",
              "type": "string"
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "format",
            "plugin_id"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "plugin"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A rack (WP-5.1): a device that holds [`Device::chains`].",
      "properties": {
        "rack": {
          "properties": {
            "kind": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/RackKind",
              "description": "Which of the four kinds of rack it is."
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "rack"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

### `DeviceLayout`

A device's layout (IMP-14): bands of controls and display cells in rows and columns.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | [`LayoutNode`](#layoutnode) | yes | The whole body. |
| `expanded` | [`LayoutNode`](#layoutnode) or null | no | The part the device adds to its body while it is expanded (L-DEV-004, L-DEV-007), if it has one: placed to the right of [`root`](Self::root). It places its parameters' controls like the rest of the layout. |

```json
}
```

| `buffer_range` | boolean | yes | Whether `buffer_sizes` is a range (its first and last values). |
| `default_buffer_size` | integer or null | yes | The buffer size it prefers, if it says. |

### `DeviceOutput`

One of a device's extra audio outputs, past its main one: `device` (an instrument on the tapped track, at any depth in its racks) and `output`, which of that device's extra outputs it is, counted from 0 in the order the device declares them.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | [`DeviceId`](#deviceid) | yes | The device. |
| `output` | integer, at least 0 | yes | Which of its extra outputs, counted from 0 past the main one. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "One of a device's extra audio outputs, past its main one: `device` (an instrument on the tapped track, at any depth in its racks) and `output`, which of that device's extra outputs it is, counted from 0 in the order the device declares them.",
  "properties": {
    "device": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/DeviceId",
      "description": "The device."
    },
    "output": {
      "description": "Which of its extra outputs, counted from 0 past the main one.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "device",
    "output"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `DevicePanel`

What the generic UI needs to draw a device (WP-2.5): its type's description and its parameters' values now.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `description` | [`DeviceDescription`](#devicedescription) | yes | Its parameters' descriptors and its layout. |
| `values` | array of number | yes | Each parameter's value now, in the description's order, in the parameter's own units. |
| `plugin` | boolean | yes | Whether this is a plug-in device's panel (WP-2.10, D19): eight knobs mapped to the plug-in's own parameters, with the rest of the body a target that opens the plug-in's editor. False for a native device. |
| `selected_slot` | integer, at least 0 | yes | For a device with sample slots (WP-5.17): the slot whose controls the panel shows, a view setting that isn't saved with the set. |
| `articulations` | array of [`Articulation`](#articulation) | no | An Articulation Map's articulations, in order: the list its panel shows. Empty for every other device. |
| `configured` | array of [`ConfiguredParam`](#configuredparam) | no | The parameters a plug-in device's panel can show, in configured order (clap-hosting R5, configure mode): a knob's context menu offers them, each over the knob it is right-clicked on. Empty for a native device. |
| `knobs` | array of integer, at least 0 | no | The knob each of the panel's parameters is drawn on, 0 to 7, parallel to `description`'s parameters (clap-hosting R5, WP-5.40): a knob's context menu remaps the knob it is right-clicked on. Empty for a device that isn't a plug-in. |
| `learning` | integer or null | no | The articulation whose Learn button is lit, counted from 0: the panel's state, not the set's. |
| `loaded_slots` | array of boolean | no | For a device with sample slots: whether each slot holds a sample. |
| `locked` | array of [`ParamId`](#paramid) | no | The parameters drawn disabled because the device takes them from its current scale: Scale's Base and Scale Name and Arpeggiator's Root and Scale, while Use Current Scale is on (the scales spec, R16). |
| `slot_keys` | array of string | no | For a device with sample slots: the key each slot plays, as Live names notes (`C3`). |

### `DeviceRole`

Where a device goes in a chain. A chain holds its MIDI effects first, then its instrument, then its audio effects, as Live's does; only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments, and a chain holds at most one instrument (a rack holds several, one to a chain).

One of:

- `"midi_effect"`: Takes MIDI and gives MIDI, before the instrument.
- `"instrument"`: Takes MIDI and makes audio.
- `"audio_effect"`: Takes audio and gives audio, after the instrument.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Where a device goes in a chain. A chain holds its MIDI effects first, then its instrument, then its audio effects, as Live's does; only MIDI tracks hold MIDI effects and instruments, and a chain holds at most one instrument (a rack holds several, one to a chain).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "midi_effect",
      "description": "Takes MIDI and gives MIDI, before the instrument.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "instrument",
      "description": "Takes MIDI and makes audio.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "audio_effect",
      "description": "Takes audio and gives audio, after the instrument.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `DisplayCell`

A display cell: a graph, a spectrum, a waveform, or an envelope editor, which grows with the room the device has. It may hold a row of controls inside its top edge and another inside its bottom edge (observed in Live 12.4.6: Compressor's display has Thresh, GR, Output, and Out along its top, and its view buttons, Knee, Look., and Env. along its bottom); they keep their size and stay pinned to those edges as the cell grows.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | What it shows, for the device that draws it and for screen readers. |
| `width` | number | yes | Its docked width, the least it has. |
| `height` | number | yes | Its docked height, the least it has. |
| `weight` | number | yes | Its share of extra room, against the other cells it shares with. |
| `bottom` | [`ControlBand`](#controlband) or null | no | Controls inside its bottom edge, from its left. |
| `slot` | integer or null | no | The sample slot the cell stands for, if it does: it shows the slot and takes a click that selects it, and a sample dropped on it (WP-5.17). |
| `top` | [`ControlBand`](#controlband) or null | no | Controls inside its top edge, from its left. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A display cell: a graph, a spectrum, a waveform, or an envelope editor, which grows with the room the device has. It may hold a row of controls inside its top edge and another inside its bottom edge (observed in Live 12.4.6: Compressor's display has Thresh, GR, Output, and Out along its top, and its view buttons, Knee, Look., and Env. along its bottom); they keep their size and stay pinned to those edges as the cell grows.",
  "properties": {
    "bottom": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ControlBand"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Controls inside its bottom edge, from its left."
    },
    "height": {
      "description": "Its docked height, the least it has.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "What it shows, for the device that draws it and for screen readers.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "slot": {
      "description": "The sample slot the cell stands for, if it does: it shows the slot and takes a click that selects it, and a sample dropped on it (WP-5.17).",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": [
        "integer",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "top": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/ControlBand"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "description": "Controls inside its top edge, from its left."
    },
    "weight": {
      "description": "Its share of extra room, against the other cells it shares with.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "width": {
      "description": "Its docked width, the least it has.",
      "format": "float",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "width",
    "height",
    "weight"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `Dither`

The noise added before rounding below 32 bits (the export spec, R7).

One of:

- `"none"`: No Dither.
- `"rectangular"`: Rectangular: noise spread evenly over one step.
- `"triangular"`: Triangular: the default, and the safest when the file will be processed further.
- `"noise_shaped"`: Noise Shaped: Beatlayer's own noise-shaped dither, for a final 16- or 24-bit render.

```json

  "description": "The noise added before rounding below 32 bits (the export spec, R7).",

    {
      "const": "none",
      "description": "No Dither.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "rectangular",
      "description": "Rectangular: noise spread evenly over one step.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "triangular",
      "description": "Triangular: the default, and the safest when the file will be processed further.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "noise_shaped",
      "description": "Noise Shaped: Beatlayer's own noise-shaped dither, for a final 16- or 24-bit render.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
```

### `EnvelopeKind`

- `"modulation"`: Moves the parameter's own value, in modulation's units.
- `"automation"`: Sets the parameter's value, in the parameter's own units.

```json
    {
      "const": "modulation",
      "description": "Moves the parameter's own value, in modulation's units.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "automation",
      "description": "Sets the parameter's value, in the parameter's own units.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```
