### `RenderedTrack`

Which track or tracks to render (the export spec, S2; WP-2.26).

One of:

- `"main"`: The Main output (post-fader sum of every track, what you hear).
- `"all_tracks"`: All individual tracks in the set: audio and MIDI tracks that make audio, group tracks, return tracks, and the Main track, one file each.
- `"selected_tracks"`: The tracks currently selected in the Arrangement: writes one file per selected track that makes audio.
- an object with `track` ([`TrackId`](#trackid)): A single track by its ID.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Which track or tracks to render (the export spec, S2; WP-2.26).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "main",
      "description": "The Main output (post-fader sum of every track, what you hear).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "all_tracks",
      "description": "All individual tracks in the set: audio and MIDI tracks that make audio, group tracks, return tracks, and the Main track, one file each.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "selected_tracks",
      "description": "The tracks currently selected in the Arrangement: writes one file per selected track that makes audio.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A single track by its ID.",
      "properties": {
        "track": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/TrackId"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "track"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SampleEditKind`

What an edit does (R55).

One of:

- `"trim"`: Keeps the selection and drops the rest.
- `"cut"`: Removes the selection and closes the gap.
- `"reverse"`: Reverses the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"fade_in"`: A straight line in gain from silence to full over the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"fade_out"`: A straight line in gain from full to silence over the selection, or the whole sample with none.
- `"normalize"`: Scales the selection, or the whole sample with none, so its largest magnitude reaches 0 dBFS.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "What an edit does (R55).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "trim",
      "description": "Keeps the selection and drops the rest.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "cut",
      "description": "Removes the selection and closes the gap.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "reverse",
      "description": "Reverses the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fade_in",
      "description": "A straight line in gain from silence to full over the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fade_out",
      "description": "A straight line in gain from full to silence over the selection, or the whole sample with none.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "normalize",
      "description": "Scales the selection, or the whole sample with none, so its largest magnitude reaches 0 dBFS.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `SampleViewChange`

How to change the Sample Editor's view: `selection` zooms to the time selection (Z), `back` goes to the view before the last zoom (X), `whole` fits the whole file across the editor (W), `height` switches fitting the waveform to the editor's height (H), `span` shows the span `start` to `end`, `scroll` shows it without remembering the view before, and `page` does the same without pausing Follow.

One of:

- `"selection"`: Zoom to the time selection.
- `"back"`: Go back to the view before the last zoom.
- `"whole"`: Fit the whole file across the editor.
- `"height"`: Switch fitting the waveform to the editor's height.
- `"span"`: Show a span.
- `"scroll"`: Show a span without remembering the view before, as scrolling does.
- `"page"`: Show a span without remembering the view before or pausing Follow, as Follow turning the page does.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How to change the Sample Editor's view: `selection` zooms to the time selection (Z), `back` goes to the view before the last zoom (X), `whole` fits the whole file across the editor (W), `height` switches fitting the waveform to the editor's height (H), `span` shows the span `start` to `end`, `scroll` shows it without remembering the view before, and `page` does the same without pausing Follow.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "selection",
      "description": "Zoom to the time selection.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "back",
      "description": "Go back to the view before the last zoom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "whole",
      "description": "Fit the whole file across the editor.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "height",
      "description": "Switch fitting the waveform to the editor's height.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "span",
      "description": "Show a span.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "scroll",
      "description": "Show a span without remembering the view before, as scrolling does.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "page",
      "description": "Show a span without remembering the view before or pausing Follow, as Follow turning the page does.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Scale`

A scale: whether Scale Mode is on (`enabled`), the root note (0 is C, 11 is B), and the scale's `name`, from the scale list. A scale with `enabled` false is the chromatic scale, whose degree is a semitone.

|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | Whether Scale Mode is on: the scale's keys are the ones the rest of the set reads. |
| `root` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The root note: 0 (C) to 11 (B). |
| `name` | [`ScaleName`](#scalename) | yes | The scale's name, from the scale list. |

### `SelectMode`

How to change the clip selection: `replace` it (a click), `add` to it, `toggle` each clip in or out (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), or `extend` it to every clip between the first selected clip and these (Shift-click).

One of:

- `"replace"`: Select only these clips.
- `"add"`: Add these clips.
- `"toggle"`: Select each clip that isn't selected and deselect each that is.
- `"extend"`: Add these clips and every clip between them and the first selected clip, in time and in the track list.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How to change the clip selection: `replace` it (a click), `add` to it, `toggle` each clip in or out (Cmd-click, Ctrl-click on Windows), or `extend` it to every clip between the first selected clip and these (Shift-click).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "replace",
      "description": "Select only these clips.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "add",
      "description": "Add these clips.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "toggle",
      "description": "Select each clip that isn't selected and deselect each that is.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "extend",
      "description": "Add these clips and every clip between them and the first selected clip, in time and in the track list.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Shape`

An automation shape: the waveforms `sine`, `triangle`, `sawtooth`, `inverse_sawtooth` and `square`, which run one cycle across the span between the bottom and top of the parameter's range; the ramps `rise` (from the value at the span's start to the top), `fall` (to the bottom), `rise_to` (from the bottom to the value at the span's end) and `fall_to` (from the top); and `adsr`.

One of:

- `"sine"`: One sine cycle, from the middle, rising first.
- `"triangle"`: Bottom to top at the span's middle and back.
- `"sawtooth"`: Bottom rising to top.
- `"inverse_sawtooth"`: Top falling to bottom.
- `"square"`: Top for the first half, bottom for the second.
- `"rise"`: The value at the span's start, rising to the top.
- `"fall"`: The value at the span's start, falling to the bottom.
- `"rise_to"`: The bottom, rising to the value at the span's end.
- `"fall_to"`: The top, falling to the value at the span's end.
- `"adsr"`: Attack, decay, sustain and release.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "An automation shape: the waveforms `sine`, `triangle`, `sawtooth`, `inverse_sawtooth` and `square`, which run one cycle across the span between the bottom and top of the parameter's range; the ramps `rise` (from the value at the span's start to the top), `fall` (to the bottom), `rise_to` (from the bottom to the value at the span's end) and `fall_to` (from the top); and `adsr`.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "sine",
      "description": "One sine cycle, from the middle, rising first.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "triangle",
      "description": "Bottom to top at the span's middle and back.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "sawtooth",
      "description": "Bottom rising to top.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "inverse_sawtooth",
      "description": "Top falling to bottom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "square",
      "description": "Top for the first half, bottom for the second.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "rise",
      "description": "The value at the span's start, rising to the top.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fall",
      "description": "The value at the span's start, falling to the bottom.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "rise_to",
      "description": "The bottom, rising to the value at the span's end.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "fall_to",
      "description": "The top, falling to the value at the span's end.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "adsr",
      "description": "Attack, decay, sustain and release.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `ShapePoint`

One breakpoint of a Shaper's shape (R23): a place in the cycle, the output there, and the bend of the segment starting at it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x` | number | yes | Where in the cycle, from 0 (its start) to 1 (its end). |
| `y` | number | yes | The output there, from 0 to 1. |
| `bend` | number | no | The bend of the segment starting here, from −1 to 1, by the automation spec's curve law; 0 is straight. |
| `sustain` | boolean | no | Whether it is the Shaper MIDI's sustain breakpoint (R26): at most one in a shape. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

      "description": "The bend of the segment starting here, from −1 to 1, by the automation spec's curve law; 0 is straight.",

      "type": "number"
    },

      "description": "Whether it is the Shaper MIDI's sustain breakpoint (R26): at most one in a shape.",

    },
    "x": {
      "description": "Where in the cycle, from 0 (its start) to 1 (its end).",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "y": {
      "description": "The output there, from 0 to 1.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "x",
    "y"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `Sidechain`

A device's sidechain input: `enabled` (the External switch), `input` (Source: `none`, or `track` with a track and a `tap`), `gain` (SC Gain, linear, 1 is 0 dB), `mix` (0 the device's own input to 1 the sidechain alone), and `listen` (Sidechain Listen: hear what the detector hears).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | no | External: whether the device's detector listens to the sidechain rather than its own input. Off on a new device. |
| `gain` | number | no | SC Gain, linear: 1 (0 dB) on a new device. |
| `input` | [`Input`](#input) | no | Source: No Input on a new device, or a track tapped Pre FX, Post FX (what choosing a track picks), or Post Mixer. |
| `listen` | boolean | no | Sidechain Listen: the device's output is what its detector hears. |
| `mix` | number | no | Mix: how much of the detector's signal is the sidechain, from 0 (the device's own input) to 1 (the sidechain alone, 100 %, as on a new device). |

```json
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "mix": {

      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

### `SliceBy`

How the dialog's Slice By chooser cuts the clip (R2, R4): a beat division, the clip's transients, or its warp markers.

One of:

- `"eight_bars"`: A slice every 8 bars.
- `"four_bars"`: A slice every 4 bars.
- `"two_bars"`: A slice every 2 bars.
- `"one_bar"`: A slice every bar.
- `"half"`: A slice every half note.
- `"quarter"`: A slice every quarter note.
- `"eighth"`: A slice every eighth note.
- `"sixteenth"`: A slice every sixteenth note: the dialog's default (R2).
- `"thirty_second"`: A slice every thirty-second note.
- `"transients"`: A slice at each of the clip's file's transients inside the region.
- `"warp_markers"`: A slice at each of the clip's warp markers inside the region.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How the dialog's Slice By chooser cuts the clip (R2, R4): a beat division, the clip's transients, or its warp markers.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "eight_bars",
      "description": "A slice every 8 bars.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "four_bars",
      "description": "A slice every 4 bars.",
      "type": "string"
    },
```

- `"previous"`: The previous take, the one above.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Which way `take_lane.replace_with_take` goes.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "next",
      "description": "The next take, the one below.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "previous",
      "description": "The previous take, the one above.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `TakeLaneId`

The ID of a take lane: a positive integer, unique within the project and never reused.

Type: integer, at least 1.

```json
  "minimum": 1,
  "type": "integer"
}
```

</details>

### `Tap`

Where a track's signal is taken: `pre_fx` before its devices, `post_fx` after its devices and before its mixer, or `post_mixer` (the default) after its pan, volume, and activator.

One of:

- `"pre_fx"`: Before the track's devices and mixer.
- `"post_fx"`: After the track's devices, before its mixer.
- `"post_mixer"`: After the track's mixer: its output. The default.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "Where a track's signal is taken: `pre_fx` before its devices, `post_fx` after its devices and before its mixer, or `post_mixer` (the default) after its pan, volume, and activator.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "pre_fx",
      "description": "Before the track's devices and mixer.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "post_fx",
      "description": "After the track's devices, before its mixer.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "post_mixer",
      "description": "After the track's mixer: its output. The default.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Taper`

How a continuous parameter's control travel maps onto its range.

One of:

- `"linear"`: Evenly in the value.
- `"logarithmic"`: Evenly in the value's logarithm, as frequencies and times are: each octave or doubling takes the same travel. Needs a range above 0.
- an object with `power` (integer from 0 to 255): As a power of the travel: the value is `min + (max − min) × nᵏ` at travel `n`, for times and rates whose knobs reach 0, such as an envelope's `32 s × n⁵`. `k` is 2 to 8.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How a continuous parameter's control travel maps onto its range.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "linear",
      "description": "Evenly in the value.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "logarithmic",
      "description": "Evenly in the value's logarithm, as frequencies and times are: each octave or doubling takes the same travel. Needs a range above 0.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "As a power of the travel: the value is `min + (max − min) × nᵏ` at travel `n`, for times and rates whose knobs reach 0, such as an envelope's `32 s × n⁵`. `k` is 2 to 8.",
      "properties": {
        "power": {
          "format": "uint8",
          "maximum": 255,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "power"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `TempoMap`

The song's tempo over time, as segments in order of position. The first starts at tick 0, each starts after the one before it, and the last is constant. A song at one tempo is a single constant segment.

Type: array of [`TempoSegment`](#temposegment), at least 1.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The song's tempo over time, as segments in order of position. The first starts at tick 0, each starts after the one before it, and the last is constant. A song at one tempo is a single constant segment.",
  "items": {
    "$ref": "#/$defs/TempoSegment"
  },
  "minItems": 1,
  "type": "array"
}
```

</details>

The tempo the audio suggests.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bpm` | number or null | yes | Beats per minute, from 40 to 240, or null if the audio is shorter than 3 seconds or has no steady pulse. A tempo far from 120 may read as half or double. |
| `confidence` | number or null | yes | How strongly the onsets repeat at that tempo, from 0 to 1. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "The tempo the audio suggests.",

      "format": "double",
      "type": [
        "number",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "confidence": {
      "description": "How strongly the onsets repeat at that tempo, from 0 to 1.",

      "type": [
        "number",

      ]
    }

  "required": [

  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `TempoSegment`

One piece of a tempo map. It runs from its start to the next segment's start; the last one runs on for ever.

One of:

- an object with `kind` = `"constant"`, `start` ([`Ticks`](#ticks)), `bpm` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)): A steady tempo.
- an object with `kind` = `"ramp"`, `start` ([`Ticks`](#ticks)), `from` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)), `to` ([`Bpm`](#bpm)): A tempo that changes in a straight line against musical position, from `from` at `start` to `to` at the next segment's start. The next segment may start at a different tempo, which makes a jump.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "One piece of a tempo map. It runs from its start to the next segment's start; the last one runs on for ever.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "A steady tempo.",
      "properties": {
        "bpm": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Bpm"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "constant",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "start": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind",
        "start",
        "bpm"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "A tempo that changes in a straight line against musical position, from `from` at `start` to `to` at the next segment's start. The next segment may start at a different tempo, which makes a jump.",
      "properties": {
        "from": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Bpm"
        },
        "kind": {
          "const": "ramp",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "start": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Ticks"
        },
        "to": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Bpm"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "kind",
        "start",
        "from",
        "to"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Ticks`

A musical position or length in ticks: 705,600 to the quarter note, so a sixteenth note is 176,400, a beat in 4/4 is 705,600, and a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400. Position 0 is the start of the arrangement (bar 1, beat 1); positions before it are negative.

Type: integer.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A musical position or length in ticks: 705,600 to the quarter note, so a sixteenth note is 176,400, a beat in 4/4 is 705,600, and a 4/4 bar is 2,822,400. Position 0 is the start of the arrangement (bar 1, beat 1); positions before it are negative.",
  "format": "int64",
  "type": "integer"
}
```

</details>

### `TimeSignatureMap`

The song's time signatures over time, as changes in order of position. The first is at tick 0 and positions increase. Each change starts a new bar; one that comes before the previous bar is full cuts that bar short.

Type: array of [`TimeSignatureChange`](#timesignaturechange), at least 1.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "The song's time signatures over time, as changes in order of position. The first is at tick 0 and positions increase. Each change starts a new bar; one that comes before the previous bar is full cuts that bar short.",
  "items": {
    "$ref": "#/$defs/TimeSignatureChange"
  },
  "minItems": 1,
  "type": "array"
}
```

</details>

### `TrackDelay`

A track's delay (the mixer spec): `{ "unit": "milliseconds", "value": 10.0 }` (−1000 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ "unit": "samples", "value": 480 }` (−192000 to 192000; kept in samples). Positive delays the track, negative plays it early.

One of:

- an object with `unit` = `"milliseconds"`, `value` (number): Milliseconds, −1000 to 1000.
- an object with `unit` = `"samples"`, `value` (integer): Samples (frames of the current sample rate), −192000 to 192000.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A track's delay (the mixer spec): `{ \"unit\": \"milliseconds\", \"value\": 10.0 }` (−1000 to 1000, two decimals; kept in milliseconds when the sample rate changes) or `{ \"unit\": \"samples\", \"value\": 480 }` (−192000 to 192000; kept in samples). Positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "description": "Milliseconds, −1000 to 1000.",
      "properties": {
        "unit": {
          "const": "milliseconds",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The delay: positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
          "format": "double",
          "type": "number"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "unit",
        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    {
      "description": "Samples (frames of the current sample rate), −192000 to 192000.",
      "properties": {
        "unit": {
          "const": "samples",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "value": {
          "description": "The delay: positive delays the track, negative plays it early.",
          "format": "int64",
          "type": "integer"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "unit",
        "value"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

```json
    },
```

```json
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "truncated": {
      "description": "Whether there were more than are listed.",
      "type": "boolean"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "count",
    "times_seconds",
    "positions",
    "truncated"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `TransportState`

What `transport.state` returns: the transport and the Control Bar's transport section, as they are now.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engine_running` | boolean | yes | Whether the audio engine runs on a device, so the transport can play. While it doesn't, the transport's commands are refused. |
| `playing` | boolean | yes | Whether the song is playing. |
| `position` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The play position (the playhead), in ticks from 1.1.1 (705,600 to the quarter note): where the song plays now, or where playback stopped, which is where `transport.continue` resumes. |
| `insert_marker` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | The insert marker, where `transport.play` starts, in ticks. |
| `arrangement_position` | string | yes | What the Control Bar's Arrangement Position fields show, as bar.beat.sixteenth by the song's time signatures: the play position while the song plays, and the insert marker while it's stopped. |
| `loop_start` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | Where the Arrangement loop brace starts, in ticks. |
| `loop_length` | [`Ticks`](#ticks) | yes | How long the loop brace is, in ticks. |
| `loop_on` | boolean | yes | Whether the Arrangement Loop switch is on. |
| `loop_start_position` | string | yes | The loop brace's start as the Loop Start fields show it, as bar.beat.sixteenth. |
| `loop_length_bars` | string | yes | The brace's length as the Loop Length fields show it: bars, beats, and sixteenths counted from 0, such as `4.0.0` for four bars. |
| `tempo` | number | yes | The tempo where the Arrangement Position fields are, in quarter notes per minute, as the Tempo field shows it. |
| `tempo_editable` | boolean | yes | Whether the tempo is one constant tempo, so the Tempo field can set it. With tempo changes along the song, change it with `song.set_tempo`'s full map instead. |
| `time_signature` | string | yes | The time signature there, such as `4/4`, as the time-signature fields show it. |
| `time_signature_editable` | boolean | yes | Whether the song has one time signature throughout, so the time-signature fields can set it. |
| `metronome` | [`MetronomeSettings`](#metronomesettings) | yes | The metronome settings: enabled, count-in, sound, rhythm, and only while recording (WP-2.15). |
| `arrangement_record` | boolean | yes | Whether Arrangement Record is on, as the Control Bar's record button shows it. While it is on and the song plays, armed tracks record. |
| `take_running` | boolean | yes | Whether a take is running: Arrangement Record is on and the armed tracks' input is being written, so playback is past the count-in and any punch-in point. It ends at the punch-out point or when recording does. |
| `counting_in` | boolean | yes | Whether the count-in is sounding, before playback and recording start. |
| `punch_in` | boolean | yes | Whether Punch-In is on. |
| `punch_out` | boolean | yes | Whether Punch-Out is on. |
| `midi_overdub` | boolean | yes | Whether MIDI Arrangement Overdub is on. |
| `automation_arm` | boolean | yes | Whether Automation Arm is on (view state, not saved with the set). |
| `automation_record_mode` | [`AutomationRecordMode`](#automationrecordmode) | yes | The mode an Arrangement recording writes control moves in, as `settings.set_automation_record_mode` sets it (the automation spec, R18). |
| `recording` | [`RunningRecording`](#runningrecording) or null | yes | The recording under way, from the moment recording starts until its clips are made; null when none is. |
| `last_recording` | [`RecordingReport`](#recordingreport) or null | yes | What the last recording that ended came to; null until one has ended in this session. |
| `capture_midi_ready` | boolean | yes | Whether Capture MIDI has notes to bring back: a monitoring MIDI track was played since the last capture or recording, so `midi.capture` runs and the Control Bar's button and Create menu item are enabled. |

### `Trigger`

How a shortcut acts.

One of:

- `"press"`: Once, when pressed.
- `"held"`: While held.
- `"latch"`: Toggles when tapped; acts only while held if held for about half a second (Live 12's momentary shortcuts).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How a shortcut acts.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "press",
      "description": "Once, when pressed.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "held",
      "description": "While held.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "latch",
      "description": "Toggles when tapped; acts only while held if held for about half a second (Live 12's momentary shortcuts).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Tuning`

A tuning: its `name`, `description`, the `cents` of degrees 1 to n above the unison (the last is the pseudo-octave), optional note `names` (one per degree) and `link`, its `reference` pitch (octave, degree and frequency in Hz) and its `range` of notes (the `lowest` on key 0 and the `highest`, at most 128 notes).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | The tuning's name: its file's name without the extension. |
| `description` | string | yes | The tuning's description, from its file. |
| `cents` | array of number | yes | The pitch of degrees 1 to n above degree 0 in cents; the last is the pseudo-octave. The pitches needn't rise in order. |
| `reference` | [`Reference`](#reference) | yes | The reference pitch. |
| `range` | [`TuningRange`](#tuningrange) | yes | The note range. |
| `link` | string or null | no | A link to a page about the tuning. |
| `names` | array of string | no | The name of each degree, 0 to n − 1, or none at all. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A tuning: its `name`, `description`, the `cents` of degrees 1 to n above the unison (the last is the pseudo-octave), optional note `names` (one per degree) and `link`, its `reference` pitch (octave, degree and frequency in Hz) and its `range` of notes (the `lowest` on key 0 and the `highest`, at most 128 notes).",
  "properties": {
    "cents": {
      "description": "The pitch of degrees 1 to n above degree 0 in cents; the last is the pseudo-octave. The pitches needn't rise in order.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "description": {
      "description": "The tuning's description, from its file.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "link": {
      "description": "A link to a page about the tuning.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "name": {
      "description": "The tuning's name: its file's name without the extension.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "names": {
      "description": "The name of each degree, 0 to n − 1, or none at all.",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "range": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TuningRange",
      "description": "The note range."
    },
    "reference": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Reference",
      "description": "The reference pitch."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "name",
    "description",
    "cents",
    "reference",
    "range"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `TuningNote`

A note of a tuning: a degree in an octave. Octave 0 starts at degree 0 of the unison; a note below it has a negative octave.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `octave` | integer | yes | The octave (a pseudo-octave of the tuning), negative below the first. |
| `degree` | integer, at least 0 | yes | The degree within it, 0 to the tuning's degrees − 1. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "A note of a tuning: a degree in an octave. Octave 0 starts at degree 0 of the unison; a note below it has a negative octave.",
  "properties": {
    "degree": {
      "description": "The degree within it, 0 to the tuning's degrees − 1.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "octave": {
      "description": "The octave (a pseudo-octave of the tuning), negative below the first.",
      "format": "int32",
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "octave",
    "degree"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `TuningRange`

A tuning's note range (the tunings spec, R8): the notes the keys play, from the lowest, on key 0, to the highest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lowest` | [`TuningNote`](#tuningnote) | yes | The note key 0 plays. |
| `highest` | [`TuningNote`](#tuningnote) | yes | The last note a key plays. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "A tuning's note range (the tunings spec, R8): the notes the keys play, from the lowest, on key 0, to the highest.",

    "highest": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TuningNote",
      "description": "The last note a key plays."
    },
    "lowest": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/TuningNote",
      "description": "The note key 0 plays."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "lowest",
    "highest"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

| `key_count` | integer, at least 0 | yes | How many keys play: 1 to 128. |

### `UnusedKind`

What kind of file an unused file is (R17): the groups the Unused Files section lists.

One of:

- `"recorded"`: Recorded into the project.
- `"imported"`: Copied into the project.
- `"processed"`: Written by an edit.
- `"other"`: Anything else.

### `UsedStretch`

A stretch of a main-lane clip that plays what a take-lane clip plays.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip` | [`ClipId`](#clipid) | yes | The main-lane clip. |
| `lane` | [`TakeLaneId`](#takelaneid) | yes | The take lane of the clip it plays. |

### `WarpFrom`

How Warp From Here warps what follows its point (the warping spec, R39).

One of:

- `"auto"`: Warp From Here: a marker on every bar after it, from the tempo found there.
- `"start_at"`: Warp From Here (Start At …): the same, starting from the tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).
- `"straight"`: Warp From Here (Straight): no markers after it, the clip's tempo the tempo found after it.
- `"bpm"`: Warp … BPM From Here: no markers after it, the clip's tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "description": "How Warp From Here warps what follows its point (the warping spec, R39).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "auto",
      "description": "Warp From Here: a marker on every bar after it, from the tempo found there.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "start_at",
      "description": "Warp From Here (Start At …): the same, starting from the tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "straight",
      "description": "Warp From Here (Straight): no markers after it, the clip's tempo the tempo found after it.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "bpm",
      "description": "Warp … BPM From Here: no markers after it, the clip's tempo `bpm` (the set's tempo there unless given).",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `WarpMode`

How a warped clip's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: the six warp modes, in the order the Audio panel offers them (R1).

One of:

- `"beats"`: Segments cut at transients or on a grid, for rhythmic material. The default of a new clip.
- `"tones"`: Grains that keep the pitch of pitched material.
- `"texture"`: Overlapping grains with some randomness, for material without a clear pitch.
- `"re_pitch"`: Plays the file faster or slower, so pitch follows speed.
- `"complex"`: Frequency-domain stretching, for whole mixes.
- `"complex_pro"`: Complex, with finer settings and Formants.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json

  "description": "How a warped clip's audio is fitted to the speed its warp map sets: the six warp modes, in the order the Audio panel offers them (R1).",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "beats",
      "description": "Segments cut at transients or on a grid, for rhythmic material. The default of a new clip.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "tones",
      "description": "Grains that keep the pitch of pitched material.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "texture",
      "description": "Overlapping grains with some randomness, for material without a clear pitch.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "re_pitch",
      "description": "Plays the file faster or slower, so pitch follows speed.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "complex",
      "description": "Frequency-domain stretching, for whole mixes.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "complex_pro",
      "description": "Complex, with finer settings and Formants.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

</details>

### `Zone`

A range of values with a fade at each end (R5): the layer is silent at the lowest and highest value when it has a fade there, and reaches full level `fade_low` values above the lowest and `fade_high` below the highest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The lowest value in the zone. |
| `high` | integer from 0 to 255 | yes | The highest value in the zone. |
| `fade_high` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | How many values the fade at the high end spans; 0 for none. |
| `fade_low` | integer from 0 to 255 | no | How many values the fade at the low end spans; 0 for none. |

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "A range of values with a fade at each end (R5): the layer is silent at the lowest and highest value when it has a fade there, and reaches full level `fade_low` values above the lowest and `fade_high` below the highest.",
  "properties": {
    "fade_high": {
      "description": "How many values the fade at the high end spans; 0 for none.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "fade_low": {
      "description": "How many values the fade at the low end spans; 0 for none.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "high": {
      "description": "The highest value in the zone.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "low": {
      "description": "The lowest value in the zone.",
      "format": "uint8",
      "maximum": 255,
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "low",
    "high"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>

### `ZoneKind`

Which of a layer's three zones.

One of:

- `"key"`: The notes it plays over, 0 to 127.
- `"velocity"`: The note-on velocities it plays at, 1 to 127.
- `"select"`: The Sample Selector values it plays at, 0 to 127.

<details><summary>JSON Schema</summary>

```json
  "description": "Which of a layer's three zones.",
  "oneOf": [
    {
      "const": "key",
      "description": "The notes it plays over, 0 to 127.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {

      "description": "The note-on velocities it plays at, 1 to 127.",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "const": "select",
      "description": "The Sample Selector values it plays at, 0 to 127.",
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```
